name: myICOR

hlido_opinion.headline: A productivity methodology sold as a membership — courses, weekly live coaching and a 9,500-member community around the ICOR system, with an app attached — but it is a training programme with an AI search box, not an AI agent.
hlido_opinion.body: Judged as what it actually is, myICOR is a coherent offering. It targets a well-defined audience (founders, owners and leaders wearing too many hats), diagnoses the problem in language that audience will recognise — notes in five places, a new tool every quarter, things slipping through the cracks — and lands on a defensible position: it isn't a tool problem, it's a missing system. The product is then structured rather than vague: a 63-lesson ICOR Journey with visible progress across four stages (Input, Control, Output, Refine), weekly live Inner Circle coaching with named coaches in your timezone, a members' community, a library, events and an app that houses all of it. The social proof is specific where most of this category is generic: 9,500+ members, 120+ countries, 900+ Inner Circle members, and an honest-looking breakdown that of 740 members who introduced themselves, 242 are CEOs or founders — a figure precise and modest enough to read as real. A free plan with 'upgrade when it clicks' is a fair offer structure, and a pricing page exists. The problem for this register is categorical. The only AI-shaped element on the captured surface is a 'Search & Ask Holista' box inside the member app; there is no agent, no automation, no API, no integration, and nothing that acts on a user's behalf. It is a coaching and education business whose software is a course-delivery and tracking app. On the axes this corpus measures — agent capability, programmatic surface, verifiable automation — there is essentially nothing to score, and the score below should be read as 'this is a competent product of a different kind' rather than as a judgement of its coaching. Buyers should also note the standard caution for this model: outcomes depend on sustained personal effort, the testimonials are vendor-selected, and no pricing figure was captured on the landing page itself.

tier_rationale: FADING (59) because the offering is clear, well structured and backed by unusually specific membership figures, but it is a coaching and course product rather than an AI agent: the only AI element on the surface is an in-app search box, and there is no automation, API or agent capability to evaluate. The score reflects its standing against this register's agent-focused axes, not the quality of the coaching, which this review did not test.
what_it_does_well: Targets a sharply defined audience and names their problem in language they will recognise
Takes a defensible position — the failure is a missing system, not a missing app — and builds the whole offering on it
Concrete structure rather than vague promise: 63 lessons across four named stages with visible progress tracking
Specific, modest-sounding social proof (9,500+ members, 120+ countries, 242 of 740 self-introduced members are CEOs or founders) rather than round marketing numbers
A genuine free plan with a stated upgrade-when-it-clicks posture, plus weekly live coaching with named coaches in the member's timezone
One app that holds courses, community, events, library and tools together instead of scattering them
what_it_fails_at: It is not an AI agent: the only AI element on the captured surface is a 'Search & Ask Holista' box inside the member app
No API, integration, automation or programmatic surface of any kind
No pricing figure on the landing page — a Pricing link exists but no tier or price was captured
Outcome evidence is testimonials and member counts; no measured result is published
Value is contingent on sustained personal effort and live attendance, which the page does not state as a condition
Listed in this register under an agent category it does not belong to
best_for: Founders and owners who have concluded that their problem is a missing operating system rather than a missing app
People who learn better with weekly live coaching and a peer cohort than from a tool
Anyone wanting to try a structured productivity methodology at no cost before paying
not_recommended_for: Anyone looking for an AI agent, automation or a programmatic tool — this is a course and community
Buyers who need the price before engaging
People who will not attend live sessions or do weekly assignments, since the model depends on both
Teams needing integrations with their existing stack
red_flags: Carried in an AI-agent register while offering no agent, automation or programmatic surface — the only AI on the page is an in-app search box
No price is visible on the landing page despite a prominent Pricing link, so the cost of the paid tiers is unknown from the reviewed surface
All outcome evidence is vendor-selected testimonials and membership counts; no measured result is offered

compared_to.verdict_diff: Tana is a working knowledge and task tool you operate yourself; myICOR is a taught methodology with an app wrapped around it. Choose Tana if you want software, myICOR if you want to be taught a system.
Mem applies AI to organising your own notes automatically; myICOR's app offers a search box and otherwise relies on you following the method. Mem is the AI product, myICOR the training programme.
